h1: The 6 Best Ultrawide Monitors for Gaming of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Ultrawide Gaming Monitors: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six ultrawide gaming monitors compared on panel type, refresh rate, contrast and price band, from VA to QD-OLED.
summary: The Alienware AW3425DW is the best overall pick, with a 240Hz QD-OLED panel. The ASUS ROG Swift PG34WCDN chases the highest refresh rate at 360Hz. Value buyers should look at the ASUS TUF VG34VQL1B, console players at the Alienware AW3425DWM, and immersion seekers at the LG 45GS95QE.
intro: The usual ultrawide mistake is paying for refresh rate your graphics card cannot feed. A 3440x1440 screen pushes about 70 percent more pixels than 1440p, so a 360Hz panel only pays off if your GPU can sustain those frames. Panel type matters more for how a game looks.
We reviewed eight ultrawides from VA to QD-OLED and ranked six by panel type, refresh rate, contrast, connectivity and price band. Rankings come from the spec sheets, not bench tests.

products.name: Alienware AW3425DW
products.verdict: The fastest 34-inch QD-OLED with a 3-year warranty.
products.description:
The AW3425DW is a 34-inch curved QD-OLED at 3440x1440, running at 240Hz with a 0.03ms response time and 99.3% DCI-P3 color. It supports G-Sync and FreeSync Premium Pro and carries a 3-year warranty.

It ranks first because it gives up only the last 120Hz of the ASUS PG34WCDN while costing the same band, $500 and up. Against the MSI QD-OLED it is 65Hz faster.

It is the pick for players who want OLED blacks and high frames on a desk-friendly 34 inches.
products.skipIf: You are on a tight budget.

products.name: ASUS ROG Swift PG34WCDN
products.verdict: The highest refresh rate in the ranking at 360Hz.
products.description:
The PG34WCDN is a 34-inch curved QD-OLED running 3440x1440 at 360Hz with 0.03ms response time. It adds DisplayPort 2.1, USB-C with 90W and a proximity sensor.

It ranks below the AW3425DW since 360Hz is only useful for competitive titles and few people can feed it at ultrawide resolution. The review sample for it is also small.

Choose it if esports performance matters and your GPU can deliver. Otherwise the Alienware is the safer buy.

products.name: LG 45GS95QE
products.verdict: A 45-inch OLED with the tightest 800R curve.
products.description:
The 45GS95QE is a 45-inch curved OLED at 3440x1440, 240Hz and 0.03ms, with an 800R curve, 98.5% DCI-P3 and G-Sync and FreeSync Premium Pro.

It ranks third because the larger size means a lower pixel density than the 34-inch models and a bigger desk footprint. What you gain is immersion without moving to 49 inches.

It suits sim and RPG players with deep desks. The sharpness of text is lower than on a 34-inch panel.

products.name: MSI MAG 341CQP QD-OLED
products.verdict: QD-OLED contrast with a shorter warranty.
products.description:
The MAG 341CQP is a 34-inch curved QD-OLED at 3440x1440, 175Hz with 0.03ms response, 1,500,000:1 contrast, HDR400 True Black and USB-C.

It ranks below the Alienware AW3425DW because it is 65Hz slower and carries a 2-year warranty instead of 3. It is the price-conscious QD-OLED, though still in the $500 and up band.

Buy it if you want OLED contrast and USB-C for a laptop. Pay more if refresh rate matters.
products.idealFor: OLED seekers who also use a laptop.
products.skipIf: You want the highest refresh rate.

products.name: Alienware AW3425DWM
products.verdict: A VA panel with a dedicated console mode.
products.description:
The AW3425DWM is a 34-inch VA curved 1500R monitor at 3440x1440, 180Hz with 1ms GtG, 3000:1 contrast and 95% DCI-P3. It has a dedicated console mode, and the listing calls it the only pick with one. It sits in the $200 to $500 band.

It ranks fifth since VA cannot match OLED blacks, but it costs far less than the OLED models.

It is the best fit for a PC and console split on a mid-range budget. Height adjustment and a 3-year warranty are included.

products.name: ASUS TUF VG34VQL1B
products.verdict: A proven 165Hz VA entry into ultrawide.
products.description:
The VG34VQL1B is a 34-inch curved 1500R VA panel at 3440x1440, 165Hz with 1ms MPRT, 4000:1 contrast and DisplayHDR 400. It is height adjustable with a 3-year warranty, in the $200 to $500 band.

It ranks last because refresh and color trail the newer picks, but it holds the highest VA contrast here.

It is the first ultrawide for buyers who want a safe, affordable option.

whatMatters.detail: VA panels give deep blacks for their price but trail OLED on contrast and motion. QD-OLED lights each pixel individually, giving near-perfect black. OLED costs more and needs care against burn-in. Choose VA for budget and OLED for image quality.

Refresh rate is how many frames per second the screen can show. A 3440x1440 panel needs a strong graphics card to reach 240Hz or beyond. Buy the rate your GPU can sustain, and check your target game's frame rate first.
A tighter curve like 800R wraps more but needs a deeper desk. 34 inches fits most desks, while 45 inches is a different footprint. Measure your desk depth before buying.
DCI-P3 coverage shows how rich colors appear. HDR True Black on OLED gives real contrast, while DisplayHDR 400 on VA is modest. Look for named HDR tiers and the DCI-P3 figure.
OLED panels carry risk of image retention, so warranty terms matter. Three years beats two. Check whether burn-in is covered on the listing.

howToChoose.intro: Pick refresh and panel by what you play.

cards.label: VA
cards.text: Affordable with strong contrast for the price, but slower pixels. Picks: ASUS TUF VG34VQL1B and Alienware AW3425DWM.

cards.label: OLED
cards.text: Near-perfect blacks and fast response, at a premium. Picks: Alienware AW3425DW, ASUS PG34WCDN, MSI MAG 341CQP and LG 45GS95QE.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers who can afford it should default to OLED, since blacks are the biggest visible upgrade.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: USB-C power delivery so one cable charges a laptop and carries video.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The ASUS PG34WCDN offers USB-C with 90W and the MSI MAG 341CQP offers USB-C too.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Motion clarity matters. The Alienware AW3425DW offers 240Hz QD-OLED over the 180Hz VA of the AW3425DWM.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You want ultrawide immersion only. The ASUS TUF VG34VQL1B sits in the $200 to $500 band.

faq.q: Does my GPU need to be powerful?
faq.a: Yes. 3440x1440 pushes about 70 percent more pixels than 1440p, so high refresh rates need a strong card.
Static images over long periods can cause retention. Vary your desktop and check the warranty, as on the Alienware AW3425DW.
Only for competitive play with matching frame rates. The PG34WCDN is for that audience.
The Alienware AW3425DWM lists a dedicated console mode.

faq.q: How should I set it up?
faq.a: Use a DisplayPort cable at the monitor's full refresh rate, and enable the sync mode in the on-screen menu.

faq.q: Can I use it for work?
faq.a: Yes. USB-C models such as the PG34WCDN simplify laptop use, but OLED text fringing may bother some users.

finalTake: The Alienware AW3425DW is the best ultrawide for most gamers, with QD-OLED quality at 240Hz and a 3-year warranty. The ASUS PG34WCDN is for esports specialists, and the LG 45GS95QE for those who want a bigger screen. On a budget, the TUF VG34VQL1B is the safe starting point.
